newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as early gains fade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as early gains fade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished weak on Thursday after early gains inspired by the Dow's strong performance and a rally in Chicago Nikkei futures overnight evaporated, dealers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 230 points lower at 18,055 after reaching a high of 18,455 soon after the open. It briefly fell below the key 18,000 support in intra-day trade.

Dealers said Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comment that he didn't view monetary policy as a tool to "prick the stock market bubble" sparked a buying spree on Wall Street, lending psychological support to the Nikkei.
News that Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) would seek to speed up the implementation of the government's plan to liberalise financial markets also provided support.
But the LDP's plan to pursue abolition of the securities transaction tax was poorly received by the market, they said.

"When people saw that, they thought the market was going to go down and it did," said a dealer with a Japanese futures house, adding that the dollar's recovery above 121.0 yen did not provide a boost to the market.
He said the March Nikkei was likely to see a slight bounce on Friday as it was looking technically oversold on the hourly charts, but he added that it would have trouble breaching Thursday's high.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 338.2 against its opening 338.5 on volume of 696 lots.
